To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
BRCA1 expression is a feature associated with higher Gleason scores and higher tumor proliferation, and is more common among men with metastatic prostate cancer at diagnosis.
BRCA1 protein is a feature of metastatic prostate cancer and is associated with worse outcomes in men who develop metastatic disease.

BRCA1 protein was expressed in 9% of primary prostate cancer and in 43% of metastatic prostate cancers; BRCA1-positive cancers were more proliferative and had higher Gleason scores; and BRCA1 positivity did not predict lethal prostate cancer among 575 men with non-metatastic disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the BRCA 1 gene in the development of prostate cancer and its progression to metastatic disease.
the role of DNA repair genes in prostate cancer progression.
the role that the tumor suppressor gene BRCA1 plays in the development of metastatic prostate cancer.
